label: ex:terminal-morphism-brings
title: Constructive terminal morphism to Bring's QOU
html:
The unique terminal morphism is constructed from any Descartes universe (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) in \mathbf{C}_{-6} to Bring's QOU (\mathbf{C}_B, A_B, \tau_B).

Step 1: Fix the substrate parameter. Objects of \mathbf{C}_{-6} are taken at a fixed value of the substrate parameter q: each carries a specialisation \iota \colon \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] \to k, and morphisms commute with these specialisations. The Descartes condition \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 constrains the base curve, not q; q ranges over its admissible values, and the local value q_0 is one of them. For source and target in \mathbf{C}_{-6} the specialisations \iota, \iota_B therefore agree, which gives an isomorphism of base rings. Define \phi_0 \colon k \to k as the identity. The terminality below is a statement for each value of q.

Step 2: Construct the monoidal functor. The fibre functor \tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathrm{Vect}_k is exact, faithful, and monoidal. By Tannaka–Krein reconstruction, the source algebra A is recovered as \mathrm{coend}(\tau^\vee \otimes \tau). Since both A and A_B satisfy the Hecke relation (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0 with identical q, the reconstructed Hopf algebras are isomorphic. Define:

  F \colon \mathbf{C} \xrightarrow{\tau} \mathrm{Vect}_k
  \xleftarrow{\tau_B} \mathbf{C}_B.

The monoidal functor \Phi = \tau_B^{-1} \circ \tau is the desired morphism on categories.

Step 3: Construct the algebra map. The functor \Phi induces a Hopf algebra homomorphism \phi \colon A \to A_B by mapping the generators of A to those of A_B:

  \phi(\alpha_A) = \alpha_B, \quad
  \phi(\beta_A) = \beta_B, \quad
  \phi(\bar\alpha_A) = \bar\alpha_B, \quad
  \phi(\bar\beta_A) = \bar\beta_B.

Both sets of generators satisfy the \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) relations. The Frobenius forms are compatible (\int_{A_B} \circ\, \phi = \int_A) because both are Haar states.

Step 4: Verify uniqueness. Suppose \phi' is another such morphism. Then \tau_B \circ \Phi' \cong \tau_B \circ \Phi \cong \tau as monoidal functors. By Tannaka–Krein rigidity, there exists g \in G_q with \Phi' = \mathrm{Ad}(g) \circ \Phi. Because morphisms in \mathbf{C}_{-6} must preserve the Haar state, and the Haar state is G_q-invariant, \int_{A_B} \circ\, \phi' = \int_{A_B} \circ\, \phi. This forces \phi' = \phi as Frobenius-algebra homomorphisms.
